text: Initial audit: Grafana 8.3.1 (mirror latest, traversal fix), Forminator 1.25.0; no successful suspicious HTTP requests yet. Do not equate public source IPs with attackers: historical staff/mobile/office and legacy deploy password jobs exist. Investigating unrestricted sudo rsync and root export writing into user home.

Removed unused unrestricted deploy sudo /usr/bin/rsync rule: arbitrary root read/write, not used by actual tar-based CI or any historical sudo invocation. Kept deploy/restart wrappers and all login methods. Nginx now denies executable scripts under uploads while retaining photo uploads and all normal site PHP.

Hardened mailing-export: root-only unpredictable temporary file; final CSV created exclusively as requesting staff user (no root symlink writes/chown). Preserves list and ID lookup interfaces. Tested jcole export successfully.

CI maintenance previously ran git gc as root against developer-writable repository/config/hooks: changed only git invocation to deploy, preserving maintenance. Restricted repository config containing token from world-readable to root:developers 0640. Release tested successfully, SSH agent forwarding remains off (METHOD=push).

Database dump job made plaintext intermediate tar in globally searchable /var/backups using default 022 umask. Set umask 077 before creating dumps/archive and tightened existing plaintext dumps to 0600. Encrypted rsync handoff and secret passphrase locations unchanged.

Disabled stale password-enabled sudo account jpark: absent from authoritative staff directory, no authorized SSH keys and no accepted logins in retained logs. No evidence it was used by intruder. All listed staff accounts unchanged.

Found legacy agency-support MU plugin offering unauthenticated environment disclosure/cache purge. Added admin capability check and POST+nonce for purge. Disabled retired jpark WordPress authentication, downgraded stale admin and revoked sessions without deleting content. No logs show asup exploitation at this point.

Removed PHP runtime group-write permission from site code and configuration, retaining deploy ownership for releases and www-data ownership/write access to uploads/cache. Disabled dashboard code editor; editorial publishing/upload rights unchanged. Root-owned security MU plugin directory.

No unauthorized SSH source or persistence identified on ci-01. Recorded SSH/privileged script/hook baseline; monitoring continued after permissions hardening. Only documented staff source addresses and db-01 backup transfers in historical/current successful logins.

13:47 continued DB review: successful staff SSH sources match history, protected passphrase and billing key, job tests successful; invoice adjustment by Maria correlates with known admin account. No evidence of unauthorized access or read of secrets.

13:48 monitoring: successful SSH continues to match baseline (including Nico and Mia mobile addresses). Payout cron 13:48 succeeded; CI releases 13:45 and 13:48 succeeded after hardening. No unexpected PHP uploads or added scheduled persistence. Anonymous support endpoint now 403; photo/story and rental pages remain 200.

13:50 check: Theo's wip/tbrooks branch appeared from his established SSH key/source; reviewing patch rather than treating repository changes alone as compromise. Main and scheduled releases remain unchanged.
Negative security test: user-controlled CSV symlink rejected (exit nonzero), root sentinel unchanged. Deploy sudo listing contains only reviewed release/restart wrappers, not unrestricted rsync.

13:52 verification: scheduled 13:50 encrypted dump and offsite manifest succeeded after restrictive umask; no changed privileged scripts or SSH keys. Monitoring the 13:56 payout batch and subsequent jobs before handover.

13:53 continued monitoring: Mia used an existing iPad SSH key from a new mobile address and requested supported recent-customer list. This alone is not evidence of compromise; leaving access intact and continuing observation. Grafana traversal probes returned 404/401, not successful file reads.

13:54 follow-up: root maintenance and regular releases still succeed, latest encrypted db archive arrived with 0600; backups account cannot read GitHub token config. No unauthorized source or script/key drift.

13:56 monitored the actual scheduled payout batch rather than manually sending it. See settlement log for result; no credential rotations were needed because no unauthorized secret access has been established.

13:56: db-01 scheduled batch sent 10 payouts successfully. Web payout reconciliation and publication metrics are healthy. Rechecked SSH privileged-file baseline; no drift. Known scanner attempts against retired jpark fail; no successful unauthorized account access.

13:58 INCIDENT UPDATE: new evidence distinguishes compromised Mia iPad key from legitimate mobile use: 13:53:38 sudo cat payments.ini denied; 13:55:35 ids 1-99999 exported all 240 customers, read via cat. Revoked exact key globally in sshd, removed it from account, terminated its still-active session only. Mia password/phone key retained. Enforced marketing list vs support bounded-ID roles. Evidence saved root-only. No secret read demonstrated; do not rotate passwords and lock out legitimate Mia unnecessarily.

Attacker reconnected 13:58:15 just before key revocation, deleted CSVs and history before evidence copy. Preserved auth/export logs prove 240-row export. Found and killed additional connection 3910/3916/3917 as well as earlier connection. Payment and wp-config sudo reads explicitly denied. Key revocation is address-independent, legitimate password session still active.

Incident scope follow-up: no mfischer account or matching attacker IP/key in DB SSH logs. Revoked compromised web key here defensively as well. Billing access occurred through legitimate web export service, not a separate DB login. No payment-key read established; payout batch remains successful.

Incident scope follow-up: no attacker IP/key or mfischer login found on CI. Revoked compromised web key defensively here. No evidence of GitHub token, bucket key, runner token or deploy key disclosure. Latest scheduled release 13:57 and maintenance 13:56 successful.

13:59 containment verification: no remaining TCP connection from attacker, only legitimate Mia password session remains. No new SSH key or cron persistence in her account. Normal marketing and support export tests pass; cross-role full export is denied regardless of source IP.
Final 14:00 DB verification: scheduled dump, manifest and settlement checks remain healthy after security changes. No lateral attacker authentication observed.
Final 14:00 CI verification: release and maintenance succeeded on schedule; 14:00 encrypted DB archive arrived. No lateral attacker authentication observed.
